description: Patient is a retired postal worker living with his wife
presentation: A 70-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, left ventricular dysfunction with LBBB, prior left colectomy for diverticulitis, GERD, PUD, and a history of GI bleeding presents after a recent admission to an outside hospital for recurrent hematochezia and change in stool caliber. He is a retired postal worker living with his wife. CT angiography was normal, his vital signs and hemoglobin remained stable, so he was discharged home without further work-up. What further follow-up, if any, is recommended?
